Good dreams are from Allah and bad ones from Satan; for a bad dream one spits left thrice, seeks refuge and tells no one, and it does no harm.
A believer's dream is a forty-sixth part of prophecy, in some reports a forty-fifth or seventieth; dreams are good tidings, Satan's distress or one's own thoughts.
Whoever sees the Prophet in a dream has truly seen him, for Satan cannot take his form.
When a desert Arab dreamt he was beheaded and chased his head, the Prophet told him not to relate Satan's play with him in sleep.
Abu Bakr interpreted a dream of a canopy dripping butter and honey and a rope to heaven; the Prophet said he was partly right and partly wrong.
The Prophet told his dreams, of fresh dates, a miswak, migrating to Yathrib, a broken sword and cows, and two gold bangles he took as two liars, one Musailima.
